title: Home Protection Plans Reinstatement Terms
content:
A cancelled plan in the Home Protection Plans line may be reinstated on its existing terms, without a new waiting period, within a limited window after cancellation.

## Terms

1. A cancelled plan may be reinstated on its existing terms without a new waiting period.
2. Reinstatement is accepted only when the customer asks to reinstate no later than the plan's reinstatement window, 30 calendar days for every plan in the line, after the plan was cancelled. The cancel date is the one shown on the company's plan record.
3. Day one is the calendar day after the cancel date, and the window closes at the end of the calendar day equal to the cancel date plus the reinstatement window in days. A request made on that last day is within the window.
4. Failures dated between the cancel date and the reinstatement date are not covered, and months skipped while the plan was cancelled are not billed.

On reinstatement the plan returns from cancelled to active, the reinstatement date is recorded on the plan, and the cancel date is cleared.

## The window, condition by condition

| Input | Judgement | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Date the customer asks to reinstate is on or before the cancel date plus the window in days | Within the window | Reinstatement accepted |
| Date the customer asks to reinstate is after the cancel date plus the window in days | Outside the window | Reinstatement not accepted |

## Boundary case (hypothetical dates, 30-day window)

Cancel date 10 June. Day one is 11 June, and the window closes at the end of 10 July.

- Request on 10 July: within the window; reinstatement accepted, with no new waiting period.
- Request on 11 July: outside the window; reinstatement not accepted.

## Gap in cover (hypothetical dates)

Cancelled 10 June and reinstated 25 June. A failure dated 18 June falls between the cancel date and the reinstatement date and is not covered.
